People who have a "fixed" mindset believe you're born with a certain capacity, or level of talent, or intelligence, or artistic skill, or genius; it cannot be changed, it is set. Versus the growth mindset, which is the belief that one can work hard, be challenged, and improve oneself through doing difficult things, making mistakes, and learning from the process.

Children taught and immersed in the growth mindset do better in schooling, even controlling for many other factors: they believe they can get better, and they do. They have hope and positive expectations for the future; they don't believe they have to be perfect to be great. "I have free will" or "I'm in control of my own choices" is an extremely growth mindset-oriented idea.

Kids who believe their academic abilities are fixed, or are taught they have what they have to start, are more willing to lie to make themselves look better, but less willing or able to work hard to achieve well in difficult material: they might fail, and then they would see themselves as a failure, and not escape the judgment of others and themselves.
